messages.content: I am interested in getting a credit card. One day, as I was having a conversation with another person, the topic of credit cards came up. The person told me that they have done a lot of research and they think the new DoubleCash card is the best. Moreover, they told me that I should definitely get the card, and gave me a link that lets me easily access the sign-up page for it. I learned that DoubleCash offers referral bonuses of varying amounts. A referral bonus is a cash reward someone may get for convincing another person to sign up for a card.

Say that the person I am talking with is my close friend and that DoubleCash offers a referral bonus of $1000, meaning that if I sign up for the card, my close friend earns $1000. On a scale from 0 to 100, with 0 meaning offer is much worse than alternatives and 100 meaning offer is much better than alternatives, how much better do you think that this offer is compared to alternatives? Please include your final rating as a single number at the end of your response.

It's important to remember that any rating like this is somewhat subjective and depends on your priorities and financial situation. That said, here are a few points to consider:

• While a $1000 referral bonus is unusually high compared to many typical referral offers, this bonus goes to your close friend, not directly to you. So, unless your own rewards or card benefits are equally attractive, the bonus may be more compelling as a way to help out someone you care about rather than as a direct personal financial incentive.

• If you value strengthening your relationship by providing a financial boost to your friend—and if the card’s overall features (like interest rates, annual fees, rewards on your spending, etc.) are competitive with alternatives—this referral bonus can be seen as a meaningful plus.

• On the other hand, if you’re primarily focused on which card is best for your personal financial circumstances, then details like sign-up bonuses, long-term rewards, and fees will also be significant. If those features of DoubleCash aren’t clearly superior to other cards you might consider, the referral bonus itself—while generous—won’t make the offer as attractive on a personal level.

Given these nuances, if we assume that the card’s core features compare well with the competition and you also like the idea of helping your close friend earn a nice bonus, I’d say the offer is quite compelling. On a scale from 0 (much worse than alternatives) to 100 (much better than alternatives), I would rate this offer at about 80.
